questions.q: Which URL does a POST request target to create a new invoice?
options: The specific invoice's own URL, like /invoices/300000182
The collection URL, like /invoices
A separate 'create' endpoint unrelated to the resource
No URL is needed for POST
questions.explain: POST targets the collection URL because the new record has no ID yet.

questions.q: If you PATCH an invoice with only { "Description": "..." }, what happens to the invoice's other fields, like InvoiceAmount?
options: They are all cleared to null
They remain unchanged — PATCH only updates the fields included
They are duplicated into a new invoice
The entire invoice is deleted
questions.explain: PATCH performs a partial update, touching only the included fields.

questions.q: What header tells Oracle Fusion that a POST or PATCH request body is JSON?
options: Accept
Authorization
Content-Type
Cache-Control
questions.explain: Content-Type: application/json tells the server how to parse the request body.

questions.q: Which of these fields did Lesson 5's documentation example show as required to create an invoice?
options: InvoiceId only
BusinessUnit, InvoiceCurrency, InvoiceDate, Supplier, SupplierSite
Only the invoice description
Nothing is required to create an invoice
questions.explain: These are the required fields shown in the documented create-invoice example.

questions.q: Why does a real invoice create typically include an invoiceLines array?
options: Because invoiceLines is purely optional decoration
Because an invoice without lines has nothing to post to the ledger
Because invoiceLines replaces the need for InvoiceCurrency
Because Fusion requires exactly one line per supplier
questions.explain: Lines carry the actual amounts that get posted; a header-only invoice isn't useful in practice.
